claim: MCTFS access create, modify and revoke move to DoD E-ICAM effective 21 September 2026 (also lines 67-68, 78; OVS 55-56, 77)
quote: Effective 21 September 2026, Department of Defense Enterprise Identity, Credential, and Access Management (E-ICAM) will replace AutoSAAR as the authoritative method to request, modify, and revoke Marine Corps Total Force System (MCTFS) end-user access.

claim: Stop submitting through AutoSAAR, email or locally routed DD Form 2875 after 17 September 2026. Verify email, phone and supervisor by 25 September 2026. Unvalidated accounts disabled 30 September
quote: Commands shall not submit new MCTFS end user access requests through AutoSAAR, legacy email, or locally routed DD Form 2875 processes after 17 September 2026
fix: Dates all fall before the 15 Nov 2026 audit date. Rewrite as past events or drop.

claim: A separated Marine retaining MCTFS access past 24 hours triggers a finding under DOD 8500.01E (also lines 81, 109, 112, 126-133; OVS 53, 82)
fix: No 24 hour disablement rule appears in DoDI 8500.01. The cited DoDD 8500.01E was replaced by DoDI 8500.01 in 2014. PAA 02-26 para 5 requires TASOs to ensure access is "terminated when personnel transfer, separate, retire" and sets no hour limit. Cite the real paragraph or call 24 hours a local standard.

claim: Revoke through Manage User Access then Remove Access; comment mandatory; system notifies IO and ISSM workgroups
quote: Requestors or their supervisors shall access E-ICAM, select the MCTFS authoritative system role source, select the required role, attach required documentation, complete the presented forms, acknowledge the request
fix: PAA 02-26 para 7 gives the request path. It names no Manage User Access menu, mandatory comment or workgroup notice. Detail sits in the DISA E-ICAM Help Guide attachment.

claim: An authorized approver (supervisor, security manager, Information Owner, ISSM) removes a role on the member's behalf
quote: Supervisors should validate the assigned role ... Information Owners and Information System Security Managers shall complete the functional and security reviews
fix: PAA lets requestors or supervisors file. It does not list the approver set for revokes.

claim: Losing command TASO deletes the User ACID at checkout; accounts cannot be reused or renamed (also 92-102, 119-121, 126)
source: MCTFS FoS Access Policy and Procedures 8.0
fix: No file for the FoS Access Policy resolves. PAA 02-26 para 5 keeps the TASO duty to support suspension, revocation or deletion.

claim: MCTFS auto-suspend at 30 days of non-use, auto-delete at 45 days; E-ICAM disables after 35 calendar days without a login
source: MCTFS FoS Access Policy and Procedures 8.0
fix: No source resolves for 30, 45 or 35 day timers. PAA 02-26 para 4.d.2 says IA certification older than a year is subject to disablement.

claim: NIS revokes on CAC deprovisioning at 3 days, unactioned Mover event at 30 days, effective 17 March 2026 (also NR 64-65, OVS 95)
fix: MARADMIN 541/26 names NIS and the 30 Sep 2027 deadline only. No file gives the 17 March 2026 release, the 3 day or 30 day triggers.

claim: Stage the audit-trail PDF in the OMPF Field Folder under the systems tab per MCO P1070.12K Chapter 3
quote: Chapter 3 contains specific information concerning the OQR and r
fix: IRAM Chapter 3 is the Officer Qualification Record. IRAM has no systems tab, no OMPF Field Folder for account closure and no death-in-service freeze rule (line 122). Cite the local SOP.

claim: DD Form 2842 is a RAPIDS workstation operator form for CAC PIN reset and DEERS access removal (account closure line 103, overview line 106, RAPIDS line 84)
fix: No DD Form 2842 file resolves in the archive (the cached DD file is DD 2875). Pages describe the form three different ways. Verify the form title and use one name.

claim: MARADMIN 541/26 retires manual DD Form 2875 on every NIPRNET system by 30 September 2027 (also OVS 59-60, 104; NR 56)
quote: execute the mandatory retirement of manual DD Form 2875 processes by 30 September 2027

claim: MOL module permissions removed per NAVMC 3500.3E T-R event 0102-GENA-1015 performance step 5
quote: 0102-GENA-1015: Manage Marine Online (MOL) modules ... Marine Online is a web-based application that provides multiple administrative tools
fix: Event is Manage MOL modules for MOS 0102 officers. Its text does not set an account-removal step. Same wrong use appears in MC lines 99 and 106.

claim: Reduction in force separation finalizes (trigger) and death in service freezes the OMPF
quote: Processing separations and retirements.
fix: MCAP does not cover account closure triggers or OMPF freezes.

claim: Submit the trouble ticket to MISSO per MCAP enclosure 6 (also 64, 86, 95)
quote: Receiving, reviewing, and submitting trouble calls beyond the MISSO's capabilities to the Manpower Information Systems Support Activity.

claim: Unit S-1 escalates a deferred case to MISSA after 5 working days; open cases past 30 days without escalation draw a finding
quote: Receiving, reviewing, and submitting trouble calls beyond the MISSO's capabilities to the Manpower Information Systems Support Activity.
fix: The MISSO escalates to MISSA, not the unit. Enclosure 6 sets no 5 working day or 30 day limit. Remove both numbers or cite the MISSO SOP.

claim: Escalations route from MISSO to MISSA per MCAP enclosure 6; MISSO and MISSA are support roles
quote: MISSOs are agencies of Headquarters Marine Corps Manpower and Reserve Affairs Department, Manpower Information System Support Division (MI).
fix: Order names MISSOs only. The Manpower Information Systems Support Activity appears as the escalation point.

claim: Route activation requests through MISSA per MCAP enclosure 6 (also 104-106, 110)
quote: Establishing unit access to manpower information systems.
fix: Enclosure 6 gives access setup to the MISSO, not MISSA.

claim: Cut a Page 11 entry per user for release training per MCO P1070.12K Chapter 6 (also OVS 78, 105; RC 67, 93)
quote: Chapter 6 adds the current authorized awards and decorations
fix: IRAM Chapter 6 is awards and decorations. IRAM 4006 limits Administrative Remarks entries to an absolute minimum. System training is not a Page 11 entry. Record training in MCTIMS.

claim: Access activated before training triggers a finding under MCO 5239.2B
quote: Ensure users and system support personnel have the required security clearances, authorization, and need-to-know, and are indoctrinated on command security practices before granting access to information systems.
fix: Order requires clearance, need-to-know and security indoctrination before access. It does not require release-specific training before activation.

claim: Every NIPRNET system completes the move to NIS on its own milestone by 30 September 2027
quote: complete NIS integration for provisioning of ICAM services with the NIS Program Office scheduled milestones for your respective systems
fix: Deadline sits on FAMs, PMs and system owners, not units.

claim: NIS released 17 March 2026 as access manager for Marine Online applications and migrated users
fix: No archive file gives the 17 March 2026 release or the user migration.

claim: Inspect two forms of ID, one government photo ID, per DODI 1000.13 Enclosure 3 (also lines 90)
quote: over 18 requires two forms of identity and refer to FIPS 201-3 and www.cac.mil, DoD List of Acceptable Identity Documents.
fix: Two-ID rule sits in DoDM 1000.13 Vol 1 and FIPS 201-3, not DoDI 1000.13 Enclosure 3. Fix the cite.

claim: Confirm the DEERS update appears within 24 hours
quote: Note: Contact the Uniformed Service DEERS Project Office if the problem is not resolved after 24 hours.
fix: Source gives a 24 hour escalation to the DEERS Project Office for support problems. It sets no DEERS posting standard.

claim: Recovered CACs are destroyed per DoDI 1000.13 recovery procedure
quote: Procedures: ID Card Life Cycle
fix: No destruction rule found in the instruction text.

claim: DD Form 1172-2 is required for CAC issuance
quote: Complete the DD Form 1172-2 or a blank computer-generated application.
fix: DD 1172-2 is the Application for ID card and DEERS enrollment (dependent and eligibility use). Source allows a computer-generated application in place of the paper form.

claim: NAVMC 10922 is the dependency application; NAVMC 10922 (EF) for DEERS dependency change
fix: Cached form text is a PDF placeholder only. Form title and instructions cannot be checked.

claim: A lost CAC needs a lost-CAC memorandum and security manager review per DODI 1000.13
quote: Procedures: ID Card Life Cycle
fix: No lost-CAC memo rule found.

claim: Submit an outage ticket to MISSO per MCAP enclosure 6 within 30 minutes; refresh status hourly; reconcile within 24 hours; stage the kit each quarter (also 65, 88, 90-91)
quote: Providing support and training for manpower information systems.
fix: Enclosure 6 sets no outage ticket time, no hourly refresh, no 24 hour reconcile and no backup kit. MCAAT findings under 5000.14D for a missing kit have no paragraph. Mark all four as local SOP.

claim: Reconcile queued transactions per MCTFSPRIUM outage procedures
fix: No PRIUM paragraph on paper outage kits or reconciliation found in the harvested set searched. Verify against the PRIUM.

claim: IPAC monitors Update and Extract Cycles for Inconsistent Conditions, Suspect Payments and Direct Deposit, and clears them before payday (also lines 59, 65)
quote: Monitor "Update and Extract Cycles" for Inconsistent Conditions, Suspect Payments, Direct Deposit participation, and ensures corrective action is completed prior to the upcoming payday as required.

claim: S-1 officer signs corrective transactions per MCAP enclosure 5 paragraph 3.b
quote: Assist commands with tracking and monitoring pay-related issues.
fix: Enclosure 5 assigns the UEC duty to the IPAC. It assigns no S-1 officer signature.

claim: Direct deposit anomaly past 30 days: escalate per DODFMR Vol 7A
quote: VOLUME 7A, CHAPTER 1: "BASIC PAY"
fix: Chapter 1 is Basic Pay. No direct deposit rule. Vol 7A is a DoD pay policy volume, not a Marine Corps Pay Instruction (line 101).

claim: A unit without a signed monthly audit draws an immediate finding under MCO 5000.14D (also lines 45, 66, 72)
quote: Complete the second stage audit after elapsed time has posted or 60 days after the join entry has processed, whichever is earlier.
fix: MCAP requires join audits, a second-stage audit at the earlier of posting or 60 days, record audits and quality control. It sets no monthly member-to-member audit or signed roster. Mark as local practice.

claim: Clear EDFR rejections within 5 working days per MCTFSPRIUM (also line 97)
quote: All DFRs, to include DFRs comprised of inconsistent conditions, will be certified by the commanding officer or the individual designated ... within 10 calendar days.
fix: PRIUM 120303: view the DFR on the date the cycle is available (next working day after a weekend or holiday). The commander or certifier certifies within 10 calendar days. No 5 working day correction rule appears.

claim: Housing allowance dependency cross-check per DODFMR Vol 7A Chapter 26
fix: Only Vol 7A Ch 1 (Basic Pay) is cached. Chapter 26 is not.

claim: Internal Control Annual Statement is required under DODI 5010.40
quote: Establishes and owns an RMIC program improvement structure ... after each statement of assurance (SOA) cycle
fix: Instruction requires a DoD annual Statement of Assurance from Components. A unit-level annual statement is a local feeder.

claim: S-1 chief is an 0111 SSgt or higher; S-1 officer is an 0102
quote: Every Marine Corps command requires administrative support and oversight.
fix: MCAP names G-1 and S-1 sections without MOS or grade requirements.

claim: Maintain rolling 12-month audit history for MCAAT
fix: No MCAAT checklist for this item in the cluster archive.

claim: Commanders impose NJP per UCMJ Article 15 and MCO 5000.14D Enclosure 3 paragraph j
quote: Submitting completed Unit Punishment Book (UPB) forms, to include results of trial by courts-martial, to the supporting IPAC.
fix: Authority comes from Article 15 and MCM Part V. Enclosure 3 para 2.j only tells commanders to send completed UPBs to the IPAC.

claim: O-3 company commander: 14 days restriction, 14 days extra duty, $200 forfeiture, reduction one grade (E-4 and below)
quote: forfeiture of not more than 7 days' pay; ... extra duties ... not more than 14 consecutive days; ... restriction ... not more than 14 consecutive days
fix: Forfeiture is 7 days' pay, not $200. Correctional custody up to 7 days is also available to any NJP authority. Reduction to the next inferior grade is limited by the imposing officer's promotion authority.

claim: O-4 and above: 60 days restriction, 45 days extra duty, half month pay for 2 months, reduction one grade
quote: correctional custody for not more than 30 consecutive days; forfeiture of not more than one-half of 1 month's pay per month for 2 months; reduction to the lowest or any intermediate pay grade ... enlisted members in pay grades above E-4 may not be reduced more than one pay grade
fix: Field grade and above may reduce E-4 and below to the lowest or any intermediate grade, and E-5 and above one grade. Add correctional custody 30 days. Line 49 repeats the O-4 row for O-5 and calls both limits equal.

claim: Evidence must be sufficient for a guilty finding beyond reasonable doubt
quote: After considering all relevant matters presented by a preponderance of the evidence standard
fix: NJP standard in the 2024 MCM is preponderance of the evidence. Rules of Evidence other than privileges do not apply (4.c.(3)).

claim: Member appeals to the next superior commander within 5 days
quote: An appeal shall be submitted within 5 days of imposition of punishment, or the right to appeal shall be waived in the absence of good cause shown.
fix: Add: appeals are in writing (7.c). The appellant may be made to serve the punishment while the appeal is pending, and any unexecuted restraint or extra duty is stayed on request if no action is taken within 5 days (7.d).

claim: Do not act on a suspended punishment until the appeal period expires or the appeal is decided
quote: A Servicemember who has appealed may be required to undergo any punishment imposed while the appeal is pending
fix: Punishment can run during an appeal. A stay applies only on request after 5 days without action.

claim: If the member demands court-martial, stop NJP. Member elects to accept NJP or demand trial
quote: Except in the case of a person attached to or embarked in a vessel, punishment may not be imposed under Article 15 upon any member of the armed forces who has, before the imposition of nonjudicial punishment, demanded trial by court-martial
fix: Add the exception. A Marine attached to or embarked in a vessel has no right to demand court-martial unless the Secretary allows it.

claim: Package begins with a charge sheet with specifications in exact MCM language
quote: The notice shall include: (1) a statement that the nonjudicial punishment authority is considering the imposition of nonjudicial punishment; (2) a statement describing the alleged offenses
fix: NJP uses a notice of the offenses and rights, not a charge sheet. Also state the right to present matters orally or in writing and to have witnesses present (4.c.(1)).

claim: Open the proceeding by identifying the member by full name and SSN
fix: No MCM rule requires the SSN. Use the EDIPI.

claim: Page 11 entry for NJP per MCO P1070.12
quote: 4006. ADMINISTRATIVE REMARKS (NAVMC 118(11)).
fix: IRAM 4006 is the right place for Page 11 entries. NJP results also go on the UPB.

claim: Reduction takes effect on the UPB date; pay changes next pay period
fix: No cached pay-effective-date source.

claim: Establishing command procedures for IPAC support is the first listed commander responsibility. Quote about free and open exchange of information
quote: Establishing command procedures for receiving IPAC support and ensuring connectivity with the IPAC. For administration to function efficiently, free and open exchange of information must exist between the unit and the IPAC.
fix: Paragraph number is 2.a, not a.

claim: 1999 consolidation moved personnel administration to IPACs and reduced commanders' access
quote: consolidation above the battalion and squadron level was directed in 1999 ... in many cases the consolidation reduced a leader's access to personnel information and processes.

claim: Commander submits accurate UMSR via MOL; timely Pro/Con marks; LIMDU documents; PEB tracking; meal card management; command payroll review
quote: Submitting accurate Unit Management Status Reports via Marine OnLine ... Reviewing the command payroll and reporting discrepancies to the IPAC.
fix: Order does not say monthly for the payroll review (line 147 adds monthly).

claim: Reserve units are supported by I&I staff, not IPACs in the same way
quote: Installation Personnel Administration Centers (IPACs) support commands and individual Marines in a defined geographic area.
fix: MCAP 11 applies to the Total Force. No I&I carve-out.

claim: IPAC positions: OIC, Personnel Officer 0170, Joins, Pay, Separations, Travel and UD/MIPS section heads
quote: Each IPAC's specific functions, organization, and support relationships will be tailored to the supported commands' mission requirements.
fix: Order tailors IPAC organization by mission. The roster is local.

claim: IPAC targets: NAVMC 10922 under 10 working days, pay error under 5 working days, separation package under 30 days, DTS voucher under 5 working days (also BP 29-37)
quote: Establish procedures for providing for receiving, monitoring, and completing, requests for assistance from supported commanders and Marines.
fix: MCAP sets no processing times. Targets in the table and in the BP table are the author's. Label them as suggested local benchmarks.

claim: Escalate to MCAAT (ask_mcaat@usmc.mil) for policy disputes
fix: No archive file carries the address (also TR line 120).

claim: BAH changes from NAVMC 10922 route S-1 directly to PAC
quote: Report Basic Allowance for Housing (BAH)/Overseas Housing Allowance (OHA).
fix: IPAC reports BAH. Direct routing is a unit choice.

claim: Standard PAC windows (NAVMC 10922 10 working days, BAH start 10, ID card 30 days, OMPF entry 30 to 60 days, Page 11 entry 30 days, travel voucher 14 days, reenlistment 30 to 60, promotion warrant 30 days)
fix: No archive paragraph sets any of these windows. Leaders will brief Marines against them. Mark them as typical local experience and not policy, or cite the source.

claim: Admin section has five working days to report an action to MCTFS via UD/MIPS
fix: No five working day UD reporting rule found in the PRIUM paragraphs searched (chapters 1, 2 and 12). Page already tells the reader to verify the local SOP. DFR certification within 10 calendar days is the nearest rule.

claim: Three-touch cadence: day 7, day 14 or window end, closure; FitRep verification at 60 days, awards at 30 to 60
fix: Leader practice with no policy source. FitReps are due at HQMC within 30 days of period end (60 days adverse) per MCO 1610.7B 3, not 60 days to OMPF.

claim: Four-level escalation ladder: named S-1 contact, S-1 chief or OIC, battalion or higher S-1, commander
quote: PARs that cannot be resolved within the command may be routed to the supporting IPAC for resolution.
fix: MCAP routes unresolved Personnel Action Requests to the IPAC. The ladder omits the IPAC and PARs.

claim: Walk or send decision table
fix: Practice guidance. No policy source expected.

claim: Commanders own the accuracy of their Marines' records (Encl 3)
quote: Commanders are responsible for the accuracy of their Marines' military records, regardless of the format of the information

claim: Marines review their own LES monthly per MCAP Enclosure 2
quote: Reviewing Leave & Earnings Statement (LES) and notifying the commander of any errors.
fix: Order says review the LES. It does not set a monthly frequency.

claim: Commanders review the unit payroll monthly per Encl 3
quote: Reviewing the command payroll and reporting discrepancies to the IPAC.
fix: Order has no monthly cadence.

claim: FSA for family separation over 30 days (contradiction flag against $250)
fix: No cached FSA source. The 30 day trigger and the $250 monthly rate do not conflict. Both belong to FSA-II. Verify rate and trigger against the statute and Vol 7A.

claim: LES posts to MyPay around the 1st of each month; review within 5 days
fix: No DFAS source cached. Marines are paid twice a month, so an LES posts on each pay date.

claim: BAS inactive for meal-card members, active for off-meal-card members
fix: Only Vol 7A Ch 1 is cached. MCO 10110.47 (BAS) appears in MCAP's directive list only.

claim: Follow up at 5, 10 and 30 days on open pay discrepancies
fix: No policy cadence. Local practice.

claim: Earn 2.5 days of leave a month, cap of 60 days at end of fiscal year
quote: Annual Leave
fix: Annual leave section is cached. 2.5 days per month and the 60 day cap are statutory. Verify at 10 U.S.C. 701.

claim: Special Leave Accrual lets you carry up to 120 days under specific conditions (contradiction flag)
quote: Marines are authorized to accrue up to 120 days earned leave when assigned to duty under the following circumstances
fix: Not a contradiction. 60 days is the normal year-end cap and 120 days the SLA ceiling for qualifying duty.

claim: Pay debts compound interest under the Statement of Service
fix: No source supports interest on pay debts compounding. Remove the sentence.

claim: Keep digital copies for at least 7 years
fix: No 7 year personal retention rule. Delete or advise keeping them until separation and VA claims close.

claim: FICA is 7.65 percent; SGLI max $500K; AFRH $0.50; DD 1561 for FSA; DD 2058 for state legal residence
fix: No archive file carries those figures or forms. Verify each against current pay tables.

claim: LES top block shows SSN
fix: Verify. Current MyPay LES truncates the SSN. MCAP Encl 2 refers to MyPay as the primary LES review route.

claim: Marines and leaders review MCTFS data via MOL; certain data (address, phone, religion) the Marine updates
quote: Certain information, such as addresses, phone numbers, and religion, can be input by the individual Marine. Changes to more sensitive information must be submitted with supporting documentation to the command or supporting IPAC.

claim: Marine updates race and ethnicity and emergency contact phone numbers in MOL
quote: Ensuring Record of Emergency Data (RED), Servicemen's Group Life Insurance (SGLI) ... are accurate and that any changes are submitted in a timely manner.
fix: Order names addresses, phone numbers and religion. Race and ethnicity are not named. RED changes are submitted (the page says S-1).

claim: MCTFS runs the PEBD Risk advisory each month through the 2nd PUREX
quote: It is anticipated this advisory will go into production in Fiscal Year (FY) 26 Quarter 2.
fix: Message announces a future deployment. Page states it as running. Confirm production date before keeping the present tense.

claim: Marine contacts the PAC or reporting unit by EPAR; provide Key Supporting Documents (DD-214s, Reserve records, orders, ROTC or academy contracts)
quote: Marines are urged to notify their servicing PAC or reporting unit, via Electronic Personnel Admin Request (EPAR), to verify and address PEBD discrepancies.
fix: Document list is not in the message. Keep it generic or cite the PRIUM.

claim: MOL permission templates that get advisories: MOL Coordinator, XO, SgtMaj, Company Commander, Company First Sergeant, Platoon Commander; PAC forwards to MMPB-21
quote: Members with one of the following MOL permission templates—MOL Coordinator, Executive Officer, Sergeant Major, Company Commander, Company First Sergeant, or Platoon Commander—will receive advisory alerts

claim: Marine responsibility beyond the advisory (paragraph 4)

claim: Corrections close in about 10 working days

claim: SGLI coverage max $500K; new SGLV-8286 to decline or reduce; NAVMC 11000 is the RED
fix: No archive file carries SGLV 8286, NAVMC 11000 or the coverage cap.

claim: Quarterly MCTFS audit, annual OMPF audit, 6 month pre-board audit

claim: Inbound records cleanup within 90 days

fix: IPAC completes join audit at reporting and a second-stage audit at the earlier of posting or 60 days. Use 60 days.

claim: Verify OMPF entry within 60 days of an approved FitRep or award
quote: Fitness reports are due within 30 days of the end of the reporting period for normal reports or 60 days for adverse reports.

claim: Corrections go to PEM Branch (MMRP) for FitReps and Awards Branch (MMPB-3)

claim: Every annual FitRep from EAS minus career back to enlistment must be present

quote: Within the first 30 days of the reporting relationship, the MRO and the RS will meet to establish and formalize a billet description for the MRO

claim: Follow-on counseling 90 days post-ICS for Cpl and above, 30 days for LCpl and below

claim: Family integration per MCO 1754.6
quote: MARINE CORPS FAMILY TEAM BUILDING (MCFTB)
fix: Order is Marine Corps Family Team Building. Page title for the reference says the same. Order covers MCFTB, not welcome or integration steps.

claim: Command Climate Surveys run per DoDI 1350.02
quote: Incorporates and Cancels: Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness Memorandum, "Command Climate Assessment," July 25, 2013
fix: Instruction absorbs the 2013 command climate assessment memo. Marine Corps execution is under MARADMIN 534/23 (DEOCS between 1 Aug and 30 Nov).

claim: Spike in NJPs over 90 days, retention drop, IG and Article 138 increases are climate indicators
fix: Indicator list has no archive source.

claim: S-1 officer signs by direction on access requests and approves privileged certifier accounts
fix: MCAP assigns no signature or approval to the S-1 officer for access requests.

claim: Validate role per MCO 5239.2B Chapter 4
fix: Chapter 4 numbering in the cached text could not be matched to the cited role-validation duty.

claim: Leader bridges a package between the Marine and the S-1, PAC, IPAC or higher admin chain
